metadata.note: Command teardown of ./art final — the dispatcher case at art:90-95 that forwards to python3 runtime/scripts/compile.py, defaulting --height 2160 when unset. compile.py is the assembler AND the review-cut compiler; --review draws beat labels and stays beside the reel, no --review writes a verified master to --out. final_preflight (paperwork triad + beat_lint + gate_shape) runs before rendering; final_frame_check (Gate V) runs against the candidate encode; approvals are re-checked and input SHA-256s re-hashed after the encode so a mid-render edit invalidates the cut. Successful finals ship with a sibling verified.json receipt (output SHA-256, input SHA-256, duration, timestamp). Slates and pending approvals block the master unconditionally; --allow-slates is review-only. All demo output in demo/RUN-LOG.txt is verbatim from this workstation against /tmp/claude-501/art-final-demo/ and /tmp/claude-501/art-final-slate-demo/. Playlist adaptation for @HumanitariansAI: composer folder chip reads @HumanitariansAI; outro card is the locked ClaudeTitleOutro with hardcoded @NikBearBrown handle per OUTRO-LOCK.md — flagged for the human reviewer before publication. No paid API, no upload, no network calls. episode.source_sha256 15dc70372375121fb4a194daa1bac7042ceb4f232345e27a08a353cd14129a10.

beats.role_note: MECHANISM — atomic candidate write pattern. Verbatim from compile.py:803-825.
beats.narration_text: The atomic bit. Compile.py encodes into a candidate.mp4 inside a temp folder next to your --out. Only after Gate V passes and the approvals recheck succeeds does the candidate get os.replaced onto the final path. If any check fails — Gate V, an approval turning stale mid-render, a source file changing hash — the temp folder is thrown away, the previous verified export stays in place, and build-state records the failure. There is never a moment when the file on disk is between two versions.

show.event: gate V + approvals recheck lines type

props.title: compile.py:803-825 — atomic replace
props.code:
# The last-good-file guarantee (verbatim, compile.py:803-825):
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(
        prefix=f'.{slug}-candidate-', dir=out_dir) as scratch:
    candidate = Path(scratch) / 'candidate.mp4'
    cmd[-1] = str(candidate)
    sh(cmd)                                    # encode into the temp
    verify_output(candidate, total, fps, …)    # decode + duration + audio
    if not a.review:
        gate = … 'runtime/qc/final_frame_check.py'
        timeline = work / 'resolved-sheet.json'
        atomic_json(timeline, sheet)           # resolved-clock sheet for Gate V
        sh([sys.executable, gate, folder,
            '--mp4',   candidate,
            '--sheet', timeline])              # Gate V on the candidate
        latest = json.loads((folder / a.sheet).read_text())
        validate_approvals(folder, latest)     # re-check approvals
        if latest != original_sheet:
            raise BuildError('Beat sheet changed during rendering…')
        if any(not Path(p).is_file() or file_digest(p) != value
               for p, value in input_hashes.items()):
            raise BuildError('Source media or narration changed…')
    os.replace(candidate, out)                 # the atomic swap
props.sparkLine: Encode into a temp. Replace only after every check clears.

beats.role_note: MECHANISM — the receipt. Five keys, machine claim only; publication is a separate human step.
beats.narration_text: The receipt is five keys. Status equals ready. Output — the absolute path. SHA-256 of the mp4. Input_sha256 — every media file and every narration mp3 hashed by name. Duration_s from the timeline the audio built. And a timestamp. Ready is a machine claim about the checks that just passed. It is not human approval, and it is not a promise of YouTube 4K processing. Publication is a separate human step.

props.title: <slug>.verified.json — the machine receipt
props.code:
# compile.py — the receipt writer (verbatim shape):
state = {
  'status':       'review' if a.review else 'ready',
  'output':       str(out.resolve()),
  'sha256':       file_digest(out),           # SHA-256 of the mp4 you just wrote
  'duration_s':   total,
  'input_sha256': input_hashes,               # {path: sha256} for every input
  'at':           datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
}
if not a.review:
    atomic_json(out.with_suffix('.verified.json'), state)
atomic_json(writable_path(folder, 'build-state.json'), state)

# Read side — downstream tooling matches file to recipe:
receipt = json.loads(Path(f'{out}.verified.json'.replace('.mp4', '')).read_text())
assert receipt['sha256'] == sha256_of(out), 'file drifted from its receipt'
# 'ready' says these automated checks passed — it does NOT mean:
#   * a human watched the film                (see FEEDBACK.md)
#   * YouTube 4K processing succeeded          (checked post-upload)
#   * professors approved publication          (out of scope for art)
props.sparkLine: Ready is a machine claim. Publication is a human step.

beats.role_note: VERDICT — six-line recap of the whole surface, in the order you use it.
beats.narration_text: So — art final. One dispatcher branch, one Python script, two verbs. It gates the paperwork, encodes into a temp, gates the pixels, re-checks approvals, and only then swaps the file in. It writes a receipt beside the mp4. Slates and pending signatures block the master unconditionally. Every guarantee — last good file preserved, receipt matches file, sheet did not drift mid-render — falls out of that same atomic pattern.

artifactLines: bare invocation — ./art final <reel> [--out DIR] [--height 2160]; forwards to python3 runtime/scripts/compile.py.
one script, two verbs — --review writes a slate-marked cut beside the reel; no --review writes a clean master to --out.
final_preflight fails fast — paperwork triad + beat_lint + gate_shape run before the first ffmpeg call.
atomic candidate write — candidate encodes into a temp, gates run against it, os.replace swaps it in; a failure never overwrites the last verified export.
verified.json is the receipt — SHA-256 of the mp4, SHA-256 of every input, duration, ISO timestamp; ready is a machine claim, not human sign-off.
slates and approvals block the master — --allow-slates is review-only, --no-gate cannot bypass approvals; a pending signature never ships.
